article.title: Contacts and lists
article.excerpt: Keep the people you message in one place, import them in bulk, and group them without duplicating anyone.

p: A contact is a name, an E.164 phone number, and optional tags. Lists are a view over tags rather than a second copy — a person can belong to several lists without being stored several times.

steps.p: This page lists existing contacts and the batches you have imported.
Map your columns to name and phone number. Numbers must be E.164.
The import lands as a batch you can inspect before you build a send from it.

sections.note: A malformed number is the most common import problem. If a contact never receives anything, check its number format in the log rather than its tags.

sections.h: Lists are a filter, not a folder
p: Because lists are built from tags, updating a tag updates every list that uses it. There is no second copy to keep in sync — which is also why renaming a list never moves a contact.
